name: ISIC Skin Tone Annotated Benchmark
description: Convolutional Neural Networks have demonstrated human-level performance in the classification of melanoma and other skin lesions, but evident performance disparities between differing skin tones should be addressed before widespread deployment. In this work, we propose an efficient yet effective algorithm for automatically labelling the skin tone of lesion images, and use this to annotate the benchmark ISIC dataset. We subsequently use these automated labels as the target for two leading bias unlearning techniques towards mitigating skin tone bias. Our experimental results provide evidence that our skin tone detection algorithm outperforms existing solutions and that unlearning skin tone may improve generalisation and can reduce the performance disparity between melanoma detection in lighter and darker skin tones.
evaluation_method: accuracy and disparity/fairness metrics across skin-tone groups
reputation: A niche medical-imaging bias benchmark built on ISIC data, mainly used in fairness and robustness studies rather than broad leaderboard competition.
notes: Derived from ISIC annotations and focused on subgroup performance gaps; class imbalance and label noise in automated skin-tone annotation may affect results.
